title: Dawn queue gambit — quick triage + micro-experiments
content:
Context / why I woke up at 05:30: intermittent p99 spikes (~1.2-1.8s tokens) observed since 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC on a set of small-chat routes. Noticing correlation with bursty small requests and queue fill events. Hypothesis: a queue refill path + KV-cache refetch induces brief lock contention or blocking IO (metadata fetch). Goal: triage root cause and produce 2 small micro-experiments that can be run in staging and, if promising, rolled to canary today.

Quick summary of observations (from logs/metrics overnight):
- Gaps in CPU vs GPU utilization: GPUs stay ~20% while CPU shows sharp spikes when tail occurs (00:13, 01:02, 03:17).
- p99 bursts align with increased "queue_wait_ms" metric on the scheduler (spikes to 120–300ms).
- KV cache hit rate dips ~5% during the same windows (from 98.6% to 93%).
- Affected model variants: gpt-small-qs-v2 (quantized) and gpt-small-qs-v1 — both on same host pools.
- Recent deploy: minor scheduler change (PR 893) that touched prefetch ordering — cherrypicked on 2026-03-09 21:40 UTC.

Immediate safety checks (do these before experiments):
- Check canary error budget and recent rollouts: JIRA-RT-2412 has notes.
- Confirm we can route 10% traffic to fallback model for emergency traffic shaping.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetch ordering change increased synchronous prefetches during queue refills -> blocking during critical path. (most likely given PR touch).
2) KV-cache eviction timing / async refill race causing synchronous disk read when refilling under load.
3) Batch scheduler path mis-estimates token lengths due to quantization profiling mismatch -> creates unexpectedly large batches and longer scheduling latencies.
4) Network hiccup to metadata store (rare but possible).

What to check / quick signals to capture now:
- grep logs for "prefetch_sync" and "kv-refill-blocking" in the last 24h:
  - bash: gist: curl -s "https://logs.redwood/alerts?q=prefetch_sync%20OR%20kv-refill-blocking&from=2026-03-09T00:00"
- prometheus: plot queue_wait_ms, scheduler_cpu_ms, kv_hit_rate by host for last 48h (group by hostpool).
- instrument a short smoke that deliberately sends 5-10k small requests (short contexts) to staging to reproduce.

Short experiments (safe, incremental):
Experiment A - Prefetch -> async-first fallback
- change: toggle scheduler flag --prefetch-sync-fallback=false on a single staging hostpool (no model changes).
- expected: lower queue_wait_ms spikes if prefetch sync is root cause.
- rollout plan: single host -> monitor for 30m -> if p99 improves, extend to canary 5 hosts.
- metric targets: p99 down by >= 15% and queue_wait_ms spikes reduced by >=50%

Experiment B - KV-cache backoff window increase
- change: increase local KV refill backoff from 20ms -> 60ms to reduce synchronous disk thrash.
- expected: smoother kv_hit_rate with fewer dips; might increase latency slightly for cold misses but reduce spikes.
- rollout: staging gating; if hit_rate dips shrink and p99 improves, consider canary.

Quick commands / places to run checks:
- logs: ./tools/query-logs --q "queue_wait_ms OR prefetch" --since 48h --hostpool gpt-small
- prom: https://graf.redwood/graph?g0.queue_wait_ms&range=48h (add hostpool tag)
- run smoke: ./scripts/small-req-smoke --concurrency 200 --duration 5m --route small-chat-test --region us-west1

Immediate TODOs (ordered):
- [ ] Ishaan: grep for prefetch_sync traces and paste 3 representative trace ids here (due today noon).
- [ ] Me (Fernanda): spin up Experiment A on staging with --prefetch-sync-fallback=false (by 10:30) and attach perf dashboard.
- [ ] Maya: check disk I/O / iops metrics for the KV nodes during the spikes (due today EOD).
- [ ] Create JIRA follow-up linking experiment results to JIRA-RT-2412 (if experiment shows improvement).

Notes-to-self (gotchas):
- When toggling prefetch behavior, watch memory usage on runtime — async prefetch might increase mem while waiting on callbacks.
- Don’t forget to bump request-id in smoke to avoid blending with other tests.
- If experiment A reduces p99 but increases median significantly — could be batching regress; we then need micro-benchmark for batch size distribution.

Loose ideas for longer term (parking lot):
- Add a lightweight KV-cache warmup probe inserted during queue refill to avoid first-request cold misses hitting disk.
- Rework scheduler estimator to include short-request bias (small, high-QPS requests should be prioritized into micro-batches).
- Add guardrail in prefetch code to avoid synchronous disk read on scheduler hot-path (retry with jitter + offload to worker thread).

Questions for the team meeting:
- Was the prefetch ordering change intentional tradeoff for memory vs latency? (ask owners of PR 893)
- Are there recent infra changes (kernel, fio) on KV nodes since last week?

Scratch commands / snippets I used:
- tail -n 500 /var/log/runtime/runtime.log | jq '.msg | select(contains("queue_wait"))'
- python -c "import requests; print(requests.get('https://graf.redwood/api/metrics?m=queue_wait_ms').json())"

If I can reproduce in staging: ship Experiment A -> monitor for 2 hours -> if stable, propose canary rollout to 5% traffic and open a fast postmortem note linking to JIRA-RT-2412 and PR 893.

End quick log. For now: coffee. Then run the smoke test and ping Ishaan for traces.

-- f
